{{Recipe}}| [[Cookbook:tea|Tea]] 

A '''Long Island iced tea''' is a mixed cocktail originating in the [[Wikipedia:Prohibition|prohibition era]] and made popular in New York speakeasies. Despite its name, the drink does not contain any tea whatsoever.

== Ingredients ==
* ¼ part [[Cookbook:Vodka|vodka]]
* ¼ part white [[Cookbook:Rum|rum]]
* ¼ part [[Cookbook:Gin|gin]]
* ¼ part [[Cookbook:Tequila|tequila]] or [[Cookbook:Triple Sec|triple sec]]
* 1 part sweet and sour mix OR [[Cookbook:Lemon|lemon]]/[[Cookbook:Lime|lime]] juice to taste
* 1 splash [[Cookbook:Cola|cola]] or [[Cookbook:Coffee Liqueur|coffee liqueur]]
* Lemon, [[Cookbook:Slicing|sliced]] for garnish

== Procedure ==

=== Shaken method ===
# Shake all the ingredients except the cola with ice in a cocktail shaker.
# [[Cookbook:Straining|Strain]] into a highball glass.
# Float the cola on the top and serve with a lemon slice.

=== Stirred method ===
# Fill a highball glass until it's almost full with ice.
# Add vodka, gin, rum, and tequila.
# Add sweet and sour mix, leaving some room on top.
# Splash in the cola and enjoy.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* Don't forget—it has to look like an iced tea, so don't add too much cola.
* To make a '''Long Beach Tea''', use [[Cookbook:Cranberry|cranberry]] juice instead of cola.
